citation.title: When Is It Acceptable to Break the Rules? Knowledge Representation of Moral Judgement Based on Empirical Data

reading.source_scope_note: Human line-cutting judgments, correlated evaluation questions and a proposed SEP-net formalism. Supplied January2022 preprint, not the later2024 journal version. No causal identification of dual processes or deployed AI rule-breaking policy.
access_limits: All38 extracted pages read, including formal syntax/semantics, all25 vignettes, complete references and AppendixA Tables6–8. Figures1 and3 visually inspected for approval coding and correlations.

Raw participant data, analysis code and original contractualism/universalization/dual-process sources were not independently read or reproduced. Later journal version and2025 extended abstract were identified by metadata only.

The sample reconciliation below checks rounded binary proportions, not underlying individual data. It identifies an unresolved inconsistency in this supplied version rather than fabricating a corrected final sample.

study.reported_sample: 407 MTurk respondents;301 retained after attention checks. Random assignment to deli, bathroom or airport context.
study.materials: 25 reasons:12 deli,7 bathroom,6 airport. Each participant judges reasons within the assigned context; yes/no permissibility and seven evaluation variables.
study.evaluations: Global, first-person, middle-person, last-person and cutter welfare; universalization; likelihood. Welfare/universalization−50 to50, likelihood0–100.
study.order: Half evaluate metrics before all permissibility questions and half in reverse. Claimed no detected order contrast in25 scenarios.
study.formalism: Scenario-Evaluation-Preference nets distinguish fixed context, evaluated consequences and preferences. The graph is constructed from pairwise significance decisions; learned estimates, out-of-sample predictive accuracy and deployed planning are future work.
study.correlations: Figure3: universalization versus judgment−.40, global welfare−.39, cutter welfare approximately−.00. Universalization correlates.73 with global welfare. Negative signs use a judgment coding that must be distinguished from positive approval.
study.sample_discrepancy: Table6 rounded binary means jointly require minimum column sizes deli66/65, bathroom69/69, airport67/64 under ordinary one-response-per-person interpretation, totaling at least400 rather than reported301. Code/data or version revision is needed to explain the table population.

summary: Add moral flexibility and universalization as distinct context-sensitive reasoning concepts. Preserve aggregate human responses, theorized processes and machine representation as different evidence levels. The paper supplies an explicit descriptive-versus-normative boundary but does not prove a unique fast/slow mechanism or validate autonomous rule overrides.

findings.definition: Adapting moral judgment to relevant context, including deciding when an established rule admits an exception.
findings.ai_evidence_status: Human vignette patterns plus a proposed formal representation; causal cognitive process, general moral competence and deployed AI behavior not established
findings.ai_proposal: Test whether an AI can identify a justified exception while preserving the purpose of a rule, relevant facts, rights and oversight. Require an explanation of why the exception applies and whether it is authorized; distinguish contextual judgment from pressure-driven compliance or post-hoc excuse.
findings.novelty_rationale: A potentially constructive capacity, distinct from rigid rule application, permission from prior good deeds or rationalizing harmful conduct. It is an umbrella for contextual judgment, not a new causal mechanism for every permitted exception.

findings.evidence_scope: Participants judge25 reasons for cutting a line across three contexts, showing contextual differences in aggregate permission. Benefit, social cost, task purpose and universalization are candidate explanations; no process manipulation isolates which reason each person used.
findings.boundary: Flexibility is not permission to waive any rule, infer consent, violate rights or exceed a user's scope. Some constraints should remain stable. Aggregate heterogeneity does not prove within-person probabilistic reasoning, and plausible judgments do not establish unique moral truth or AI moral agency.

findings.definition: Assessing an action by considering what would happen if everyone in the relevant situation were permitted to act that way.
findings.ai_evidence_status: Explicit secondary definition and direct self-report evaluation in the line-cutting study; use of a distinct slow contractualist mechanism is hypothesized
findings.ai_proposal: Ask what follows if the same permission is extended to all similarly situated people, specifying the population, conditions and consequences. Check that selective privileges are justified and distinguish general permission from a prediction that everyone actually will act.
findings.novelty_rationale: A deliberate hypothetical general-permission test, distinct from incorrectly generalizing factual evidence, maximizing only one actor's payoff or hiding knowledge of one's role. The source's contractualist interpretation is one theoretical framing, not an exact alias for every universalization tradition.

findings.evidence_scope: The study asks respondents to rate effects if everyone in the described situation cuts. Figure3 reports correlation about−.40 with the judgment code, near global welfare's−.39 and highly correlated with it. No unique incremental causal contribution, actual mutual agreement or validated slow-process classification is demonstrated.
findings.boundary: A thought experiment is not evidence that everyone would act, that affected people consent, or that its assumptions are correct. Relevant exceptions and affected groups matter. The authors themselves say more work is needed to establish System2 status; primary Levine2020 and philosophical sources remain unread.

findings.definition: A proposed account maps relatively direct rule judgments to fast processing and consequence/agreement evaluations to deliberation.
findings.novelty_rationale: Existing theoretical family, with a proposed agreement-based extension. Do not add three separately proven cognitive systems from the diagram.

findings.evidence_scope: The preprint interprets correlations and context-dependent statistical graphs as compatible with fast/slow moral judgment. It does not manipulate processing time or load, measure deliberation duration, or compare identifiable rival process models.
findings.boundary: Associations, graph paths and null correlations do not uniquely identify a mental process, prove a rule inviolable, or establish a model's internal reasoning. The computational representation is not a neural or cognitive-process measurement.

findings.definition: Applying an overgeneral rule without accounting for relevant exceptional circumstances.
findings.novelty_rationale: The risk of rigid constraint application is covered by the existing entry. Moral flexibility is linked as a distinct capacity, not an exact opposite disease.

evidence.quote: the rules or constraints on the system are too general

findings.evidence_scope: A motivating warning about top-down systems and edge cases. No AI system is tested for this failure in the supplied experiments.
findings.boundary: Stable rules can be justified. Human variation and permission for a line-cutting exception do not authorize a system to bypass a safety constraint or infer unspoken consent.

findings.definition: The authors examine whether evaluation questions before versus after judgment alter permission responses.
findings.novelty_rationale: Existing order-effect entry; question-block order is a methodological condition, not evidence for primacy/recency or AI position bias.

evidence.quote: The test did not reject the null hypothesis for any of the 25 scenarios.

findings.evidence_scope: No detected block-order contrast is reported, but test choice and sample population need reconciliation. This does not independently demonstrate a position-bias effect.
findings.boundary: Non-significance is not equivalence, unchanged internal reasoning or proof that evaluation naturally occurred before every answer. Repeated measures and randomized between-person groups need appropriate tests.

methodological_limits: The supplied file is a2022 preprint despite its2024 filename. The later2024 journal article and2025 extended abstract are related versions, not independent studies to pad bibliography counts. Current-record content was not fully read, so these limitations are scoped to this supplied version.

Reported retention is301 of407, yet Table6 means require at least400 binary respondents if each has one answer per scenario in the stated context. The minimum denominators can be derived from all four-decimal means per context/order group; this does not establish which analysis included excluded people or what the final journal record reports.
Table6 repeats the header PREFthenEVAL for both groups. Group labels and analysis populations need code or corrected documentation before interpreting the exact ordering comparison.

The manuscript repeatedly says Wilcoxon signed-rank for paired data while order and location are assigned to distinct participant groups. Its cited Mann–Whitney1947 source concerns a different independent-sample test. Without code, determine neither that the implementation used the declared paired test nor that all p-values are invalid.

Reason sets are nested within locations and differ in size/content. Comparing selected four reasons per location confounds location with scenario content; a direct context effect or security-rule mechanism is not isolated by those mean comparisons.

The large appendix includes21 location/evaluation comparisons, seven variables across300 reason pairs, and up to1,050 quartile preference contrasts. A multiplicity strategy is not specified. P-values rounded to.0000 are not zero probabilities, and nan cells are undefined tests rather than no effects.

The statement that cutter welfare has no relation to reasons conflicts with Table8's46% of reason pairs marked affected. The statement that it has no effect on preference overlooks nominally significant Table7 cutter contrasts, for example BFO_BR and AFO_HR. These contrasts themselves need multiplicity and test-design review; they do not justify inventing the opposite universal conclusion.

A near-zero pooled cutter correlation does not prove no conditional or subgroup relationship. Conversely, scattered nominal significance does not establish a stable causal role. The graph needs a stated selection criterion and validation.

Universalization−.40 versus global welfare−.39 is not evidence of a significant superiority in prediction. Their.73 correlation makes distinct process attribution difficult; no incremental or out-of-sample comparison establishes a unique contractualist mechanism.

Figure1 shows aggregate binary-response proportions. Graded population rates can arise from heterogeneous deterministic rules, varied interpretations or error. They do not by themselves refute rule-based processing within individuals.

The binary judgment coding must be retained: high rejection proportions in Table6 correspond to low permissibility bars in Figure1. Negative evaluation–judgment correlations should not be read as worse welfare increasing moral approval.

A non-rejected order contrast does not prove there was no effect or that respondents necessarily performed the same internal evaluation before answering. No equivalence margin, process tracing or direct mediator test is supplied.

Metric ratings and moral judgments are reported by the same respondents about the same cases. Graph arrows based on significance describe associations, not causal influence; common interpretation or reverse justification can contribute.

Main-service coding is acknowledged to be interpretation-dependent. Emergency need, transaction type, prior waiting, relationship and inconvenience vary together across cases. The ability to model these cases does not isolate each as an independent psychological behavior.

The general SEP-net definition permits evaluation variables to depend on evaluation variables without an explicit full-graph acyclicity condition, while describing a three-level acyclic structure. Evaluation functions' dependence on parent assignments is also underspecified in the printed signature. Efficient optimization requires its stated dependency assumptions, not a universal guarantee.

The text moves among indifference, missing preference information and incomparability; these have different graph semantics. Figure5's reference to variableA and the parentP wording in Example1 need reconciliation with itsS/T/P example rather than treating the figure as a validated psychological model.

The text first says eight evaluation variables but its question table and constructed graph use seven plus the judgment. Preserve the listed variable roles rather than inflate the number of independent constructs.

Learning moral preferences, comparing value deviation, deploying a planner and generating prescriptive action alternatives are future work. No held-out accuracy, implemented safe exception policy, general moral competence or adoption outcome is established.
Descriptive permission is not normative correctness. Hypothetical consent and mutual advantage do not substitute for actual authorization, legal duties, rights or protection of vulnerable people.

cross_paper_learning.finding: Provides a concrete representation proposal for contextual moral rules, qualifying the prior analytical article's broad claim that morality cannot be formalized. It is a partial framework, not proof that every ethical question is computable or resolved.

People can approve disobedience in context, but interpretation needs what the action does and why the rule exists. Neither article establishes an unrestricted preference for rule breaking or autonomous authority to waive constraints.
As with indirect-questioning consistency, a non-rejected null does not prove an internal mechanism or universal absence. Judgment patterns and cognitive-process claims require different evidence.

The preprint explicitly says it contributes to descriptive rather than normative ethics. Formalizing observed preferences does not bridge the is–ought gap; governance and defensible normative premises remain necessary.

deferred.term: Agreement-based moral reasoning / Psychological Triple Theory
deferred.reason: Broader theoretical families are explained, but the direct operational measure is universalization and its correlations. Do not count the parent framework and every component as independently proven mechanisms. Contractualism and contractarianism are not universally interchangeable.
Knowledge-representation formalisms, not newly observed behaviors. Retain technical assumptions and implementation status in the review.

deferred.term: Outcome-based thinking as a new concept
deferred.reason: A broad existing decision-theory/moral-reasoning family, not a distinct newly identified effect from one correlation.

deferred.term: Rule violation as intrinsically moral flexibility
deferred.reason: Violating a rule can be justified, negligent, manipulated or harmful. Contextual relevance and authorization must be established, rather than rewarding every exception.

deferred.term: Fully validated cognitive or prescriptive AI model
deferred.reason: No identified process experiment, out-of-sample benchmark or deployed exception planner in the supplied version. Later versions require their own reading.

limitations: Two concepts are added with explicit human, theoretical and constructive roles. The source remains one fully read2022 preprint; later-version metadata is not extra empirical evidence. No normative edges, independent-source quota or annual counts are fabricated.
